title: Speculative decoding + model integration: acceptance, rollback, metrics (draft)
content:
Status: Draft (internal review).

Overview:
This document sketches the integration plan for speculative decoding into the Redwood serving runtime and defines acceptance criteria, rollback procedures, and the metrics/telemetry we will use to evaluate safety, latency, and quality tradeoffs. It covers interactions with kernel selection, request scheduling, and KV cache semantics. This is a working doc — expect open questions and TODOs.

Goals:
- Add speculative decoding support to runtime with minimal disruption to existing SLOs (p50/p95 latency, throughput).
- Provide model-integration checklist for accepting a model/binary that enables speculative outputs (including quantized variants).
- Define safe rollback paths and automatic abort conditions.
- Define metrics and dashboards required to make informed rollout decisions.

High-level approach:
1) Runtime hook points: speculative decoding will be implemented as an optional path in the token-generation pipeline. Hook points: generation scheduler (decide speculative candidate generation), kernel selection (fast fallback kernels), KV cache access (speculative cache entries vs canonical).
2) Scheduler: introduce a spec-decoder-aware scheduler policy that can: a) decide fraction of requests to run speculative (based on route/model, traffic tier), b) limit additional GPU concurrency budget for speculative work, c) fall back to synchronous path if resource constrained.
3) Kernel selection: best-effort fast kernels (lower-precision or trimmed attention) will be used for speculative candidate generation; canonical kernels used for final scoring if needed. Kernel metadata must include "speculative-safe" flag.
4) KV cache semantics: speculative decoding can produce KV cache entries that are tagged as provisional. Provisionals must not be pinned to long-lived sessions until confirmed by final generation or consensus; eviction and cache-coherence rules must account for mixed provisional/canonical states.

Model integration checklist (for teams onboarding models that opt-in to speculative decoding):
- Model artifacts: provide performance profiles for baseline and speculative kernels (latency/throughput at relevant batch sizes and sequence lengths).
- Quality tests: automated eval set (task-specific) showing metric delta between canonical and speculative outputs (perplexity, BLEU/ROUGE/EM as appropriate, LLM evals).
- Determinism: document nondeterministic behaviors introduced by faster kernels/quantization and expected variance bounds.
- Fallback compatibility: model must support fallback to canonical path without semantic/format changes.
- KV cache correctness tests: unit tests for provisional KV insertion, read-after-write semantics, and session recovery.
- Safety checklist: toxicity and safety evals on speculative outputs; thresholds for blocking rollout.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before canary -> broader rollout):
- Performance: end-to-end p95 latency for nominal route must not degrade >5% at target load with speculative enabled at default traffic fraction.
- Resource usage: additional GPU memory and compute for speculative workload < 20% of baseline per-request cost (configurable by policy).
- Quality: automated eval delta for primary metrics (task-dependent) within defined bounds (e.g., <1.5% absolute drop for top-line metric) and no systematic regressions on safety tests.
- Error rates: no increase in server error rate (5xx) or decode-level errors (truncation, malformed tokens) beyond baseline noise.
- Cache correctness: no session-level KV corruption observed in end-to-end smoke tests across simulated failures and restarts.
- Observability: dashboards and alerts built for all key signals (see metrics section) and verified in staging.

Rollback plan and abort conditions:
- Gradual rollout: start with 0.5% of production traffic on a controlled route -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% if all gates pass. Each step requires manual/automated gating.
- Canary monitoring: continuous evaluation on live canary traffic with automatic rollback if any of the following triggers:
  * p95 latency increase >10% sustained for 5m
  * end-to-end error rate increase >2x baseline for 5m
  * quality regression on shadow evals exceeding thresholds (see acceptance)
  * evidence of KV divergence (mismatched session state)
- Fast rollback path: spec-decoder feature flagging at router and worker level to immediately stop sending speculative tasks; worker-internal graceful termination to let in-flight speculative batches finish or be dropped by policy.
- Full revert: if rollback at feature-flag level insufficient, deploy hotfix to revert kernel selection changes and re-enable canonical-only path. Pre-built revert PRs must be available before canary begins.

Metrics and telemetry (required):
- Latency & throughput: per-route p50/p95/p99 for both speculative and canonical paths; tail latency broken down by kernel type.
- Resource metrics: GPU utilization, memory pressure, additional ops/sec introduced by speculative tasks.
- Quality metrics: task-specific accuracy metrics, perplexity, response divergence rate (percent of speculative responses that differ from canonical on deterministic tests).
- Safety metrics: toxicity scores, rate of flagged responses.
- Error metrics: 5xx, decode failures, malformed outputs, KV cache inconsistencies (measured via session hash comparisons in shadow runs).
- Economic metrics: tokens generated per request, incremental cost per request with speculative enabled.
- Rollout telemetry: fraction of traffic spec-enabled, per-customer opt-outs, policy decisions taken by scheduler (why a request was not speculated).

Dashboard & alerts (minimum):
- Speculative overview: traffic fraction, success/fail counts, mean extra compute per spec request.
- Quality regression alert: automatic daily eval on sampled traffic; alert if rolling 1h delta exceeds threshold.
- KV divergence alert: any session-level mismatch > 0 in production triggers SEV.

Operational considerations:
- Backpressure: speculative tasks must be schedulable with a separate concurrency budget to avoid starving canonical work. Implement token-bucket style limiter per-GPU and per-queue.
- Cost control: allow per-customer and per-route policies to opt-out or cap speculative work; default off for low-tier customers.
- Debugging: provide request-level tracing that includes which kernels used, provisional KV IDs, and scheduler decision logs. Traces must be linkable to stored request payloads for replay.
- Testing: extensive simulated load tests and shadowing run comparing canonical vs speculative outputs at scale before canary.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to unify provisional KV semantics with cross-worker session migration? (session affinity implications).
- Exact thresholds for quality delta depend on product use-case; need product input for default thresholds per route.
- Need to formalize how provisional KV eviction interacts with long-running conversations and streaming.
- Decide if speculative outputs should be cached for reranking use-cases (yes/no per-route).

Implementation milestones (proposed):
- M1 (2 weeks): runtime hooks, feature flag, basic scheduler policy + unit tests.
- M2 (3 weeks): kernel tagging + selection logic, provisional KV tagging and basic correctness tests.
- M3 (2 weeks): metrics instrumentation, staging canary harness (shadow mode).
- M4 (2 weeks): closed beta with partner internal routes, finalize acceptance automation.
- M5 (1 week): public rollout and postmortem window.

Notes: This doc is intended to be practical and implementation-focused. Please add comments inline or push PRs against the design repo.

Next steps: schedule design review with serving-runtime, applied-ml, and console teams; agree on canary gating automation; create revert PRs and run staging shadow at ~50k QPS equivalent to validate tail behavior.
